# P4 Parity Variance — Electron Aggregation vs Backend Aggregation

**Phase**: P4 (plan.md "Parity") | **Date**: 2026-09-04 | **Fixture**: `torrent-streamer/internal/catalog/testdata/parity/parity-fixture.json` (single source consumed by both implementations)

**Method**: golden fixtures exported from the Phase 1 renderer characterization fixtures (Frieren scenario). The renderer golden (`testdata/parity/renderer-rows.json`) is GENERATED by `electron-app/scripts/parity/renderer-catalog.mjs` running the real characterized modules (`src/lib/anime-catalog.ts`, `src/lib/adapters/media.ts`) — expected outputs derive from characterized behavior, not from the backend implementation. The Go parity suite (`internal/catalog/parity_test.go`) feeds the identical payloads through the real adapters and compares.

## Parity proven (tests green)

| Dimension | Parity test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| No data loss: every renderer-kept row has a backend row with the same normalized title+year key | `TestParityRendererRowsAppearInBackendRows` | PASS |
| Identifier mapping: backend `providerIds` contains each renderer row's provider-local id | `TestParityRendererRowsAppearInBackendRows` | PASS |
| Anime classification: renderer `isTmdbAnime` (ja + genre 16) matches backend `Type == anime`; non-anime rows classify movie/series identically | `TestParityAnimeClassificationMatchesRenderer` | PASS |
| Cross-provider join: TMDb + AniList + Jikan rows for the same work join into exactly one merged backend row | `TestParityDroppedTMDbAnimeRowsAreMergedNotLost`, `TestParityJikanOnlyInBackend` | PASS |
| Determinism: same payloads ⇒ byte-identical backend ids/ordering across runs | `TestParityBackendOrderingIsContractDeterministic` | PASS |

## Reconciliation notes

- No backend defects were found requiring code changes: the characterized renderer behaviors that the spec preserves (anime classification rule, title normalization key, dedupe-by-canonical-work outcome) are reproduced by the backend merge. The divergences above are all consequences of explicitly specified V2 contract evolution (client-neutral merged rows), not mismatches.
- V4 note: the renderer's "drop TMDb anime rows" rule would LOSE works that AniList does not know; the backend's merge keeps them (joined when AniList knows them, standalone otherwise). This is a strict improvement in coverage and is required by the merge determinism contract; it is not a silent behavior change.
- Regeneration: `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/parity/renderer-catalog.mjs ../torrent-streamer/internal/catalog/testdata/parity/parity-fixture.json ../torrent-streamer/internal/catalog/testdata/parity/renderer-rows.json` (run from `electron-app/`); re-run whenever the characterization fixtures or renderer aggregation modules change.
